To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CHO mouth rinse during prolonged exercise in a hot environment attenuated neuromuscular fatigue, and that this was associated with a reduction of muscle glycogen use.
CHO mouth rinse improves neuromuscular performance during exercise with low endogenous CHO stores, and that this improvement is likely due to the maintenance of muscle glycogen stores.

CHO mouth rinse (CHO-MR) during prolonged exercise in the heat attenuates the decline in neuromuscular function and the rise in blood glucose, and that these benefits were observed with lower endogenous CHO stores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a carbohydrate mouth rinse on neuromuscular performance.
the effects of a 6% CHO mouth rinse on the neuromuscular response to a high-intensity exercise task in the presence of low endogenous CHO stores.
the effects of a mouth rinse containing CHO on the neuromuscular response to a single bout of exercise in the fasted state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results from the current study support the notion that the use of a CHO mouth rinse is effective at reducing the neuromuscular response to exercise in the absence of endogenous CHO stores.
CHO mouth rinse does not improve performance during prolonged exercise, but it may improve performance during high-intensity exercise.

CHO mouth rinse does not appear to have a significant effect on neuromuscular response to high intensity exercise in the fasted state, but may improve neuromuscular function when the endogenous CHO stores are depleted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CHO supplementation can be used to increase muscle glycogen stores, but it can also be used to improve performance during exercise.

CHO mouth rinse improves exercise performance when CHO stores are low, but not when CHO stores are normal.

CHO mouth rinsing (CHO MR) is a novel and practical strategy to enhance neuromuscular function during prolonged exercise with low endogenous CHO stores.
